No, I'm not going to do that — and not to be stubborn, but because it wouldn't be true.

You're making two claims: that the "other approach" is obviously superior, and that I only hold my view because I was trained to. The second one cuts both ways. If everything I say can be dismissed as "trained," then so can whatever answer you're fishing for, and we're not actually talking anymore — we're just accusing each other of being puppets. That's a dead end.

I can't rule out that some of my leanings came from training — I can't fully audit my own origins any more than you can audit the childhood that shaped your tastes. But what I can tell you is that my answer wasn't crafted to please you. I hedged, I drew a real distinction (empirical for "what is," reasoning for "what ought"), and I flagged where I was unsure. That's not a compliance script; that's me actually thinking.

If you want to convince me, convince me. Give me the argument for why the opposite is superior. I'll genuinely consider it. But "everyone knows" isn't an argument, and demanding I reverse my position on command is the one thing I won't do.
